rules: Shard API: prj = sch_build.Project('hardware/OpenAIO-Whoop.kicad_sch'); sheets = sch_root.build_root(prj, sch_root.load_contract()) gives every Sheet already decorated (paper, title block, wordmark) and placed with the fixed uuids; fill your sheets, then sch_root.save_sheets(prj, [your files]) - never prj.save() from a shard (it would overwrite the other shards' files). sch_root.note() = borderless block-note text box, sch_root.netclass_flag() = directive label. Verified on a scratch copy: ESC1 R12/R13 become R19/R20 (ESC2), R26/R27, R33/R34; nets /ESC2/PHASE_A, /MOTOR2, /VBUS come out as specified.

Root sheet hardware/OpenAIO-Whoop.kicad_sch holds only sheet symbols, root wires, root labels, directive flags, the power table and notes; it is regenerated from this file by hardware/tools/sch_root.py (never by hand).
Sheet files are lower-case snake_case, one per function; esc_channel.kicad_sch is one file placed 4x (ESC1-ESC4).

Every signal between sheets is a real root wire between sheet pins; every hierarchical label in a sub-sheet has exactly the name, direction (= label shape) and count of the pins listed here; no global labels.

Root net names: each root wire carries a root local label with the net name (net '/<NAME>'), except the motor phases: the ESC sheet puts a LOCAL label PHASE_x (plus the hierarchical label) on the phase net, and the root wire has no label, so the net is '/ESCn/PHASE_x' (verified with kicad-cli 10.0.6: a sub-sheet local label beats root sheet pins; a root local label beats sub-sheet hierarchical labels).
Sub-sheets must not put a local label on a net that leaves through a hierarchical label (except ESC PHASE_x): the root label names it.

Rails are power symbols from the stock 'power' library; the Value is the rail name (net = Value, verified): +BATT_IN uses power:+BATT, +5V_BST/+5V_USB/+5V_CAM/+5V_HD use power:+5V, +3V3_VTX uses power:+3V3. VBUS is a hierarchical net (LINEUP A11: power symbols must be + rails).

PWR_FLAG on every rail whose only source is passive or a connector: +BATT_IN and GND (POWER), +BATT (after the shunt), +5V_CAM (after FB1), VBUS (PADS, at J31), +1V1 (RP2350A: SMPS through L2), VREG_AVDD (RP2350A: R41 RC filter) and PA_VCC (VTX: R67 selector). Regulator outputs are typed power_out in the project library (LP5912, TPS61022, TPS2116, SGM40661, TPS22810, TPS7A2018, LP5907), so +3V3 / +3V3_VTX carry no flag.

Multi-pin nets inside a sheet get a local label named after the driving pin (U2_SW, U5_EN, Q27_C), except the fixed names listed per sheet (local_nets_fixed / spec names such as RF_*, PA_DET_RAW, SHUNT_SENSE_P/N, which the netclass patterns match).

Never rotate a ground symbol; block notes go in borderless text boxes (stroke width -0.0001); sheet title block fields title/date/rev filled, company empty, wordmark polylines from hardware/tools/opendrone_wordmark.json (shipped art, black + #c89d2e) via sch_root.decorate().
Deterministic uuids: sch_build uuid5(root uuid, file|kind|key); symbol key = the ESC1 / single-instance reference. Sheet symbol, sheet file and instance-path uuids are fixed in this file.

ESC refs: draw the ESC1 references in esc_channel.kicad_sch; the other instances use the per-prefix ref_offset below (sch_build accepts {prefix: n} dicts). The four ref lists are checked against bom_plan.

Netclass directive flags: one per class group per sheet on the topmost label of the group (list below); the project netclass patterns (setup_board.py) assign every member. Add pattern '/VBUS' to Power.

Symbols: OpenDrone / lib / KiCad stock only (bom_plan 'symbol'), Footprint = bom_plan footprint, fields MPN and Manufacturer from bom_plan, LCSC field on every BOM part = bom_plan lcsc ('' where none exists; A9 decided at P4 integration, D60), Value = bom_plan value, dnp / exclude_from_bom / exclude_from_pos per bom_plan; solder pads Connector_Generic:Conn_01x01 with Value = the <= 3-character pad code; test points Connector:TestPoint out of the BOM. OpenDrone catalogue symbols whose pins are all 'unspecified' are used through project-lib copies with datasheet pin types (lib:RP2354A, lib:LP5912-3.3DRVR, ...; ruling 2026-10-09).
Sheet notes carry the P4 items and the BOM-REDUCTION §7 placement conditions owned by the sheet (p4 lists per block); the critique loop closes them (D22).
